text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up: I'm proposing we embed a tiny, versioned shard metadata header inside safetensors to speed up fast warmup paths. This would be an optional header that the runtime can parse without fetching a sidecar manifest. Thoughts?

alex: Short pros/cons from my side — pros: single-file atomic transfer helps edge caches and cold-starts. Cons: header bloat and harder to patch metadata without republishing whole checkpoint.

kevin: What exactly would go in the header? shard id, per-layer offsets, checksums, quantization layout flags? size matters here. Maybe keep it to offsets + digest + format version + warmup-priority hint.

sara: Also consider the update story. If we want to patch priorities or rollout metadata, sidecar manifest is easier. Could support both: embedded header for "hotstart hints" and sidecar as authoritative manifest.

maria: That was the idea. Proposal sketch: optional 8KB "warmup header" chunk in safetensors. Contains: offsets for first N tensors, a per-shard priority hint, a small checksum (sha256 ref), and a format version. Runtime reads it sync to produce a WarmupPlan; background validation against sidecar manifest remains required.

alex: Failure modes we should enumerate: header present but out-of-date vs manifest; origin doesn't support range requests; corrupted header. Need clear ABI and a compatibility flag.

kevin: Example header (pseudo):
```
{
  "version": 1,
  "shard_id": "shard-042",
  "warmup_ranges": [[0, 65536], [131072, 196608]],
  "priority": "hot",
  "digest_ref": "sha256:abcd..."
}
```
This is intentionally minimal. Keep binary encoding compact in real impl.

deploy-bot: RFC PR #2378 posted with ABI sketch and loader state machine: https://git.redwood/eng/rfcs/2378 (please review)

sara: Security question: if header can influence prefetch, we must avoid cache-poisoning. Need signatures or provenance tag so Dedicated/private runtimes can choose to trust.

maria: Agreed. Add fields: signed_digest_ref and namespace. Also runtime config: `trust_embedded_header=false` by default; opt-in per-namespace or via release rollout.

alex: Operational note: Dedicated and Private can set policy to trust headers for perf. We should add telemetry: header_used, manifest_verified, reconcile_result; log for 2-4 weeks before flip.

kevin: Implementation plan for loader: on open -> read magic + header_len -> parse header -> produce WarmupPlan (prioritized byte ranges) -> schedule async validation: fetch sidecar manifest and reconcile. If mismatch, evict warmup entries and rehydrate from manifest ranges.

sara: Edge-case: origin lacks range support. Header helps a lot there, but watch out — header may give false confidence if we can't actually fetch ranges efficiently. Runtime should detect origin capability and degrade gracefully.

maria: I'll draft a short follow-up RFC with ABI bytes layout, state machine, and migratory plan. Owners: maria (spec), kevin (loader impl), alex (telemetry/policy), sara (security/signing). I'll include a microbenchmark plan.

alex: :thumbsup: Can you add a small perf microbenchmark to the warmup harness (measure latency to first token under header vs manifest-only)?

maria: Yep — will include in PR. Timeline: draft RFC by EOD Friday, implementation spike next week.

sara: Sounds good, thanks everyone.

maria: Thanks — ping me if you want to pair on the ABI.
